question: Is about 30% of Gulf oil settled in yuan?
start: PIIE (M. Chorzempa), 2 September 2026: yuan share of SWIFT payments peaked at 4.7% in July 2024 then fell to 2.75%. Official data put China's goods trade settled in yuan at 28% in the first half of 2025

links.claim: The yuan is about 2.75% to 3.1% of SWIFT payments in 2026, sixth or fifth place. China's own goods trade settled in yuan was 28% in the first half of 2025 on official data

evidence.what: PIIE: SWIFT share 4.7% peak July 2024, 2.75% after. 28% of China's goods trade in yuan, first half 2025. CIPS about 33,000 transactions a day, 210 direct participants

links.claim: The specimen's 'about 30%' is most likely China's own yuan trade-settlement share (28%) relabelled as a Gulf oil figure, a definition swap
footprints_expected: A Gulf-specific 30% figure from Aramco, ADNOC, SAMA, CBUAE or a tracker would have to exist if the claim were measured
Gulf sources (the mirror) would report large yuan receipts
A matching 28 to 30% figure in a Chinese aggregate

footprints_found.what: PIIE: 28% of China's goods trade settled in yuan, first half 2025
Argaam 2026 piece on the petroyuan gives no share and names no yuan cargo

footprints_missing: No Gulf-specific yuan share found in three searches (Aramco, ADNOC, SAMA, S&P, Argaam)
S&P Global says yuan use remains limited in Saudi-China oil trade
rivals: The 30% is a real private estimate for China's total crude import bill, inflated by Russian and Iranian barrels that are paid largely in yuan, then misapplied to the Gulf
A real but unpublished Gulf figure exists, for example yuan paid on some UAE cargoes through CIPS or mBridge
links.reveal: SWIFT tracker each month. Aramco annual report for 2026, March 2027. PBoC RMB internationalisation report, about September 2027. Any Aramco or ADNOC statement of yuan settlement

links.claim: Accounting bounds the claim. 30% of all Gulf crude sales would be over 100 billion dollars a year in yuan, which the visible Gulf yuan plumbing (CBUAE swap line 35 billion yuan, about 5 billion dollars) and falling CBUAE reserves do not show. 30% of the Gulf's sales to China alone (about 35 billion dollars a year) cannot be ruled out if converted at once
footprints_expected: A yuan stock or large swap drawings on SAMA or CBUAE books
Gulf bank yuan claims in BIS locational data
Swap lines sized near the flow

footprints_found.what: CBUAE renewed a 35 billion yuan (18 billion dirham) swap with PBoC in November 2023 for five years
CBUAE gross reserves fell 12.4% from February to August 2026, with an equity definition break in March

footprints_missing: SAMA currency mix not reachable. BIS yuan claims by Gulf banks not pulled. No SAMA-PBoC swap figure found this search
rivals: Yuan received for oil is spent at once on Chinese imports and never sits on a balance sheet, so no stock appears
Yuan is held by Aramco, ADNOC or commercial banks, not the central bank, and would show only in BIS data
links.reveal: BIS locational banking statistics by currency, third quarter 2026, late January 2027. SAMA monthly bulletin if reachable

links.claim: SAMA left the mBridge cross-border platform after its proof of concept ended on 13 May 2025 (reported September 2026), so one yuan settlement channel for Saudi oil is not in use by SAMA

evidence.what: Crowdfund Insider citing SAMA and the FT: Saudi Arabia ends public role in mBridge after the trial (via EXAM_T9)

rival_hypotheses.text: Oil is priced and mostly settled in dollars. Yuan use is small and case by case
Gulf exporters and China agreed to move about 30% of oil to yuan
Some sellers take yuan where they buy Chinese goods, without any wider agreement
Measurement: a China-wide 28% trade figure, or a Russia and Iran heavy figure, was read as a Gulf oil share
